entities.name: Jiong of Xia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Jiong of Xia was the twelfth king of the semi-legendary Xia dynasty, reigning from approximately 2200 to 2000 BCE in ancient China. His reign is marked by the development of bronze technology and the establishment of a hierarchical system of government. The Xia dynasty's existence has been the subject of debate among historians, with some arguing that it may have been a mythical era. Despite this, Jiong's legacy as a king who oversaw the growth of the Xia dynasty's power and influence remains significant. The Xia dynasty's impact on Chinese history cannot be overstated, and Jiong's reign is an important part of this narrative. The discovery of the Shang dynasty's oracle bones in the 19th century provided evidence of the Xia dynasty's existence, although the details of Jiong's reign remain shrouded in mystery. The Xia dynasty's influence can still be seen in modern-day China, and Jiong's legacy serves as a reminder of the enduring power of ancient Chinese dynasties.
